To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the upper urinary tract dynamics of patients receiving urinary reservoir operations were not influenced by the presence of the reservoir, but the reservoir was more likely to be associated with renal injury in patients with abnormal waves on CMGs.
the patterns of diuria renography of full reservoir were different from those of the empty reservoir in 5 of 5 patients with abnormal waves on CMGs, but not in the 9 patients without.
diuresis renographic findings of patients with intestinal urinary reservoir were worse during full reservoir than empty reservoir in patients with abnormal waves on CMGs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the effects of a new method of treatment for the prevention of urinary tract infection.
the evaluation of upper urinary tract function in patients with intestinal urinary reservoir.
the study of the upper urinary tract dynamics using diuresis re-nography in the patients with the reservoir operation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diuresis renograms are not a reliable method for evaluating the upper urinary tract in patients receiving an urinary reservoir operation.

diuresis renographies with full and empty reservoir are useful to assess upper urinary tract dynamics in patients with an ileal conduit or an ileal reservoir, and that the results of diuresis reno- graphy with an empty reservoir should be interpreted with caution.
diuresis renograms with empty reservoir should be performed routinely in patients with urinary reservoir.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diuresis renographic findings with full reservoir are worse than those with empty reservoir only in patients with abnormal CMG waves.
diuresis renographic evaluation during full reservoir is necessary in patients with intestinal urinary reservoir and/or bladder augmentation.
the diuresis reno- graphy with full bladder is more sensitive than CMG in detecting upper urinary tract dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

diuresis renograms should be performed in patients with urinary diversion or augmentation, and if abnormal waves on cystometrogram are detected, diuresis renographies should be performed during empty reservoir.
diuresis renograms with the reservoir empty and full can be useful to assess the upper urinary tract dynamics in patients who have undergone urinary reservoir surgery.
patients with intestinal urinary reservoir and abnormal waves in CMG should be carefully followed.
